Pasvitinys Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiauliai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Before 1862, when the local Jewish community purchased its own burial ground, Pasvitinys's Jews used the Jewish cemetery in nearby Joniskis instead. The community, settled likely at the end of the 18th century, peaked at 435 people (57 percent of the town) by 1897; by 1931, all nine shops in town were Jewish-owned, though a 1930s economic crisis and open anti-Jewish propaganda drove significant emigration to South Africa, America, and Israel. In 1941, the town's Jews were imprisoned in an old barn, taken out daily for farm labor, and eventually transported to Žagarė, where they are believed to have been murdered alongside that town's own Jewish community on October 2, 1941 — one of several communities from this region who met the same fate at that site. Though the cemetery was never demolished, no organized community remained to care for it after the war; descendants now periodically visit in search of their roots, and through their efforts some gravestones have been restored.
